title: Deterministic contract coverage
summary: Agents creating or modifying machine-checkable normative contracts MUST assign policy ownership and deterministic automation or validator coverage.
instructions: This rule covers a new or changed normative requirement for an output shape, required artifact, traceability relationship, deterministic operation, or machine-checkable invariant. The agent MUST identify its owning policy and a registered automation or validator id. When the registry capability does not yet exist, the agent MUST include an explicit implementation specification instead.

A handbook rule MUST apply broadly across repository work. An invocation-specific requirement MUST live in a policy, a workflow stage, or a prompt instead. A handbook addition MUST be high-signal and MUST NOT duplicate an existing authoritative rule without a concrete retrieval benefit.
Validator and automation definitions MUST live in one canonical registry. Policies and applicability rules MUST reference stable ids and MUST NOT duplicate executable paths or command definitions.

The harness MUST derive applicable automation and validation requirements from the policies resolved for an invocation. Agents MUST NOT maintain them in an independent second applicability map that can drift from policy selection.

instructions.text: Repository validation MUST fail for a missing policy owner, unknown requirement id, duplicate registry id, missing executable, or invalid target declaration. It MUST also fail for a policy-bound requirement whose executable contract cannot resolve once the registry capability is active (`registry-validate`).

instructions: An agent MUST mark a requirement that cannot be checked deterministically as judgment-only with a rationale. The agent MUST NOT represent it as covered by a superficial structural validator.

instructions.text: The harness MUST treat the repository-local `.cursor/` directory as ignored, disposable configuration. That directory MUST NOT contain authoritative Pancreator functionality (`projection-validate`).

`governance/registries/projection_manifest.json` MUST declare every Pancreator-owned Cursor agent, command, or rule projection. Its canonical implementation MUST live under `library/` or `src/`. Installers and sync automation MUST NOT read the source checkout's `.cursor/` directory as authority (`projection-validate`).

Repository validation MUST validate canonical projection sources and manifest coverage independently of whether a local `.cursor/` projection exists. When a local projection exists, repository validation MAY report drift with the registered regeneration command (`projection-validate`).

The context-bloat disposition record MUST cover each detected duplicate group and installer monkeypatch through the registered directive-audit requirement. The record MUST give a rationale and evidence for each retained exception (`directive-audit`).

Embedded installation and refresh MUST place Pancreator-owned ignore patterns in the target clone's `.git/info/exclude` through the managed installer block. They MUST NOT create, rewrite, or remove target `.gitignore` content, and MUST preserve unrelated clone-local exclude content. They MUST keep the managed block idempotent across refreshes (`tests/secondary/embedded-installation.test.ts::embedded installer stays out of target git state`).

instructions: Generated invocation manifests MAY persist resolved requirement ids, versions, paths, arguments, targets, and failure routes for auditability. Agents MUST receive only the entries relevant to the active invocation.
Required plan-file child fields MUST declare their shape and registered validator enforcement in the shared stage-output requirements contract.

A worker MUST write its stage output after its last edit to every claimed path. An edit to a claimed path after the output write makes that output stale; coverage: `tests/integration/validators-stage-validators.test.ts::a claimed path modified after the output fails, and an ordered one passes`.

instructions.text: Every field a stage validator blocks on MUST appear in that validator's `enforced_fields` and in the shared contract's `fields[]`; repository validation MUST fail on a missing declaration (`tests/integration/policies.test.ts::repository validation rejects a verify field omitted from enforced_fields`).
